Adding a number charges its activation to your payment method right away.

post.description:
Send a typing indicator from the number identified by ``alias``.

The sender is the number in the URL ``alias``. The ``from`` body field
is not required, and when supplied it is ignored (the URL always wins).

With ``is_typing`` true, the number first appears online and the unread
messages it received in that conversation are marked as read, then after
a short random pause (between 0.3 and 1.5 seconds) the typing indicator shows,
so it never shows over unread messages. With ``is_typing`` false only
the indicator is cleared and nothing is read.

422.description: The request has a value that is not valid.

post.description:
Mark a chat's (or WhatsApp Group's) unread inbound backlog as read
from the number identified by ``alias``, independent of the
automatic mark-as-read that already accompanies send, reply, react,
edit, delete and the start of the typing indicator (the number also
appears online first, and goes back offline by itself a few minutes
after its last interaction). Useful for
a customer's own client that wants inbox parity (e.g. an unread
badge cleared by the user) without sending any WhatsApp message.

The sender is inferred from the URL ``alias``; there is no ``from``
body field.

phone_number.title: Phone Number
phone_number.description: The phone of the number, in international format (for example `+5511988887777`).

external_id.title: External Id
external_id.description: Optional. Your own identifier for this number (1 to 128 characters). Another number of your account already using it answers 409 `external_id_already_used`, and nothing is charged.

external_id.title: External Id
external_id.description: Your own identifier for this number, for example the id of the customer it serves in your system. 1 to 128 characters, surrounding spaces removed, no control characters. Unique among the numbers of your account; `null` when not set. Unlike `alias`, it can be any text (a UUID or an integer sent as a string) and it does not change when you rename the number.

ContactListResponse.title: ContactListResponse
ContactListResponse.description:
List of contacts plus an opaque next cursor.

``cursor`` is the token to pass back as ``?cursor=...`` on the next
request; ``null`` when there are no more contacts. ``has_more`` says the
same thing as a boolean (``true`` exactly when ``cursor`` is not
``null``), to keep pagination loops simple.

ContactQuotaResponse.title: ContactQuotaResponse
ContactQuotaResponse.description:
A number's current contact-quota snapshot.

The quota counts the current billing cycle, from ``cycle_start`` to
``cycle_end`` (the same shape as the message quota). ``resets_at``
always equals ``cycle_end``.

These three fields are UTC timestamps with second precision and a ``Z``
suffix, the same format used by the ``contact.quota.*`` webhook events
and every other timestamp in the API (for example ``at`` on message
responses).

.. code-block:: json

   {
     "used": 87,
     "quota": 1000,
     "remaining": 913,
     "cycle_start": "2026-06-01T00:00:00Z",
     "cycle_end": "2026-07-01T00:00:00Z",
     "resets_at": "2026-07-01T00:00:00Z",
     "tier": "SOLO"
   }

ContactRefreshPayload.title: ContactRefreshPayload
ContactRefreshPayload.description:
The last refresh you asked for on this contact.

``completed_at`` and ``outcome`` stay ``null`` while the refresh runs.

ContactResponse.title: ContactResponse
ContactResponse.description:
One contact.

``picture`` says whether the contact's profile picture is available
(``kind``: ``"available"`` or ``"unavailable"``); ``null`` when the
picture has not been checked yet.

ContactSource.title: ContactSource
ContactSource.description:
How a contact first appeared. It never changes afterwards.

Values:
    inbound: the first message came from this contact.
    outbound: the first message was sent to this contact.
    mention: the contact was first seen in a mention (in a message
        received, sent from the phone or sent through the API).
    self: the contact is one of your own numbers (main or extra).

ContactUsageSnapshot.title: ContactUsageSnapshot
ContactUsageSnapshot.description: Contact-quota section of the usage response.

EventResponse.title: EventResponse
EventResponse.description:
One event of the events list, with the same fields as the webhook.

- ``id``: the event id (``evt_...``).
- ``type``: the event type, for example ``message.received``.
- ``organization_id``: your organization id (``org_...``).
- ``number_alias``: the number the event belongs to (``"main"`` or the
  alias of an extra number); absent on organization-wide events.
- ``created_at``: when the event was recorded (ISO 8601).
- ``data``: the event payload, identical to the one the webhook delivers.

external_id.title: External Id
external_id.description: Your own identifier for this number, for example the id of the customer it serves in your system. 1 to 128 characters, surrounding spaces removed, no control characters. Unique among the numbers of your account; `null` when not set. Unlike `alias`, it can be any text (a UUID or an integer sent as a string) and it does not change when you rename the number.

ExtraNumberSummaryResponse.title: ExtraNumberSummaryResponse
ExtraNumberSummaryResponse.description:
One number of the account in the list.

Fields in order: `contact_id`, `name`, `type`, `alias`, `number`,
`external_id`, then `description` and `status`.

external_id.title: External Id
external_id.description: Your own identifier for this number, for example the id of the customer it serves in your system. 1 to 128 characters, surrounding spaces removed, no control characters. Unique among the numbers of your account; `null` when not set. Unlike `alias`, it can be any text (a UUID or an integer sent as a string) and it does not change when you rename the number.

GetExtraNumberStatusResponse.title: GetExtraNumberStatusResponse
GetExtraNumberStatusResponse.description:
One extra number, with its status and, while pairing, its code or QR.

Fields in order: `contact_id`, `name`, `type`, `alias`, `number`,
`external_id`, `status`, `at`, then `description`, `scheduled_deletion_at`,
`reason` and `pairing`.

external_id.title: External Id
external_id.description: Your own identifier for this number, for example the id of the customer it serves in your system. 1 to 128 characters, surrounding spaces removed, no control characters. Unique among the numbers of your account; `null` when not set. Unlike `alias`, it can be any text (a UUID or an integer sent as a string) and it does not change when you rename the number.

GetMainNumberResponse.title: GetMainNumberResponse
GetMainNumberResponse.description:
The main number of the account and its status.

Fields in order: `contact_id`, `name`, `type`, `alias`, `number`,
`external_id`, `status`, `at`.

GetMessageDetailsResponse.title: GetMessageDetailsResponse
GetMessageDetailsResponse.description:
One message, with the same fields as the ``message.*`` webhook events.

Common fields:
- ``id``: the message id (``msg_...``).
- ``organization_id``: your organization id (``org_...``).
- ``number_alias``: the number the message belongs to (``"main"`` or the
  alias of an extra number).
- ``from``/``to``: sender and recipient; their shape depends on the
  direction.
- ``preview``: the first characters of the message (up to 50). It is kept
  only for your plan's content retention period, like the content itself.
- ``content_type``: ``text``, ``image``, ``audio`` and so on.
- ``direction``: ``"outbound"`` or ``"inbound"``.
- ``channel``: always ``"whatsapp"``.
- ``origin``: ``"tn"`` (sent through the API) or ``"native"`` (sent or
  received on WhatsApp itself). Always present, never ``null``.
- ``at``: when the message happened on WhatsApp (ISO 8601). It does not
  change as the delivery state advances.
- ``status``: ``{state, at, error}``. ``status.at`` is when the current
  delivery state was reached. ``error`` (``{code, message, hint}``) is
  present only when ``state`` is ``"failed"``.
- ``mentions``: the ``@<number>`` mentions found in the text or caption,
  in order, as ``[{contact_id?, name?, number}, ...]``; absent when the
  message mentions nobody. Kept after the content retention period ends.

Content fields (one, matching ``content_type``):
- ``text``: the full text, for ``content_type="text"``.
- ``image``, ``video``, ``audio``, ``document``, ``sticker``: the media,
  with a ``media`` block that says whether the file is available
  (``kind`` field).
- ``location``: ``{latitude, longitude, name?, address?, ...}``.
- ``calendar``: ``{name, start_at, ...}``.
- ``interactive``: ``{interactive_type, body, header?, footer?, url_button}``.
- ``replied``: ``{message_id, preview}``, on a reply.

For a reaction, ``content_type`` is ``"text"`` and ``text`` holds the
emoji (``""`` when the reaction was removed).

GroupListResponse.title: GroupListResponse
GroupListResponse.description:
List of groups plus an opaque next-page cursor.

``cursor`` is ``null`` when there are no more groups. ``has_more`` says
the same thing as a boolean (``true`` exactly when ``cursor`` is not
``null``).

GroupResponse.title: GroupResponse
GroupResponse.description: One WhatsApp group the number belongs to.

InteractiveHeaderInput.title: InteractiveHeaderInput
InteractiveHeaderInput.description: Header of an interactive message. Only a text header is supported.

MessageError.title: MessageError
MessageError.description:
Structured error for a failed message operation.

The same shape is used everywhere a failure is reported: the webhook
``data.error`` of failed events and the ``status.error`` of the message
endpoints (``GET /v1/messages/{id}``, ``GET .../status`` and the
send/edit/delete/reply responses). Present only when the message state
is ``failed``; ``null`` or absent otherwise.

Fields:
    code: Stable machine-readable identifier. Branch on this value (for
        example ``media_fetch_failed``, ``unsupported_media_format``,
        ``reaction_lid_unavailable``). It is never translated or reworded.
    message: Human-readable summary of what went wrong.
    hint: Actionable remediation guidance. Omitted, never ``null``, when
        no guidance applies.

MessageListResponse.title: MessageListResponse
MessageListResponse.description: Cursor-paginated list of messages for one number inbox.

These three fields are UTC timestamps with second precision and a ``Z``

NumberFamilyUsage.description:
``used``, ``quota`` and ``remaining`` of one quota on one number.

``resets_at`` and ``tier`` are the same for every number of the
organization, so they appear once, at the top level of the response.

OrganizationListResponse.title: OrganizationListResponse
OrganizationListResponse.description:
The organization of the API key, as a list.

Your key belongs to one organization; exactly one is returned.
``cursor`` is always ``null`` and ``has_more`` is always ``false``.

OrganizationResponse.title: OrganizationResponse
OrganizationResponse.description: The organization that owns the API key used in the request.

OutboundRecipientInput.title: OutboundRecipientInput
OutboundRecipientInput.description:
The recipient: a phone number, a group or a contact.

Send exactly one of:
- ``number``: the phone in E.164 format, for a one-to-one message.
- ``group_id``: a group id (``grp_...``), to send to a WhatsApp group.
- ``contact_id``: a contact id (``ct_...``); the message goes to that
  contact's phone.

Sending more than one, or none, is rejected with 422 ``invalid_recipient``.

OutboundSenderInput.title: OutboundSenderInput
OutboundSenderInput.description:
The sending number, given by ``alias`` or by ``number``.

Send exactly one of them: ``alias`` (``"main"`` or the alias of an extra
number) or ``number`` (the phone in E.164 format). Sending both, or
neither, is rejected with 422.

PairExtraNumberRequest.title: PairExtraNumberRequest
PairExtraNumberRequest.description:
Optional body of the pairing request.

An extra number is always paired with a pairing code that you type in
WhatsApp (Linked devices, Link with phone number instead), so
`pairing_code` is the only accepted method and the body can be left out.
Any other value answers 422.

ProfilePictureAvailable.title: ProfilePictureAvailable
ProfilePictureAvailable.description:
Profile picture is accessible via a signed URL.

``url_expires_at`` is set for temporary (signed) URLs and ``null`` for
permanent public URLs. After a temporary URL expires, fetch the contact
again to get a fresh one instead of keeping the old URL.

``hash`` is the hex-encoded SHA-256 of the picture bytes. It stays the
same when the same image is uploaded again, which helps to deduplicate.

``fetched_at`` records when the picture was last fetched from
WhatsApp, useful for freshness heuristics.

ProfilePicturePending.title: ProfilePicturePending
ProfilePicturePending.description:
Profile picture upload to organization storage is in progress.

``hash`` may be present when the SHA-256 of the fetched bytes is
already known while the upload is in progress.

ProfilePictureUnavailable.title: ProfilePictureUnavailable
ProfilePictureUnavailable.description:
Profile picture cannot be served.

``reason`` vocabulary:

* ``"no_storage"``: the organization has no object storage configured.
  ``setup_hint`` is always present.
* ``"upload_failed"``: the upload failed after all retries.
  ``setup_hint`` is ``null``.
* ``"peer_has_none"``: the contact has not set a profile picture.
  ``setup_hint`` is ``null`` (nothing to set up on your side).
* ``"storage_circuit_open"``: uploads to the storage are paused after
  repeated failures. ``setup_hint`` is present.

``setup_hint`` is present exactly when ``reason`` is ``"no_storage"`` or
``"storage_circuit_open"``.

PublicNumberStatus.title: PublicNumberStatus
PublicNumberStatus.description: What a customer reads in a number's `status`.

ReactionFromPayload.title: ReactionFromPayload
ReactionFromPayload.description: The ``from`` party of a reaction item.

ReactionItem.title: ReactionItem
ReactionItem.description: A single active reaction to a message.

ReceiptFromPayload.title: ReceiptFromPayload
ReceiptFromPayload.description:
The party who emitted a delivery/read receipt.

``number`` is ``null`` when WhatsApp does not reveal the phone of the
person who acknowledged. The ``from`` object is still returned when
``contact_id`` or ``name`` are known even without a phone number.

ReplyMessageRequest.title: ReplyMessageRequest
ReplyMessageRequest.description:
``POST /v1/numbers/{alias}/messages/{message_id}/reply`` request body.

Both recipient (``to``) and sender number are inferred: the recipient
comes from the original message direction; the sender is the ``{alias}``
URL segment.  Only ``content`` is required.

scheduled_deletion_at.title: Scheduled Deletion At
scheduled_deletion_at.description: When the number is removed. The current time when it was removed right away; otherwise the end of its paid period, until which it keeps working.

refund_eligible.title: Refund Eligible
refund_eligible.description: ``true`` when the number was removed right away and its activation charge is refunded. ``false`` when the removal is scheduled for the end of the paid period, with no refund.

refund_amount_cents.title: Refund Amount Cents
refund_amount_cents.description: Amount refunded to your payment method, in cents of your billing currency. 0 when there is no refund.

refund_status.title: Refund Status
refund_status.description: Outcome of the refund when the number was removed right away: `succeeded` (the amount is on its way back to your payment method), `not_applicable` (there was nothing to refund) or `failed` (the number is removed and our billing team completes the refund). Null when the removal is scheduled.

ScheduleExtraNumberDeletionResponse.title: ScheduleExtraNumberDeletionResponse
ScheduleExtraNumberDeletionResponse.description: What removing the number did: removed right away with a refund, or scheduled.

SendAudioContent.title: SendAudioContent
SendAudioContent.description:
Send an audio file or voice note via a public URL.

WhatsApp does not show captions on audio, so this content has no
``caption`` field (a caption would be silently lost).

SendCalendarContent.title: SendCalendarContent
SendCalendarContent.description:
Schedule a calendar event as a WhatsApp event message.

``start_at`` and ``end_at`` are timezone-aware ISO-8601 datetimes
(values without a timezone are rejected).

SendContactContent.title: SendContactContent
SendContactContent.description:
Share a contact card as a WhatsApp contact message.

You send the structured fields below and the vCard is built for you, so
the card always opens correctly in WhatsApp. You never write a vCard yourself.

SendContactEmail.title: SendContactEmail
SendContactEmail.description: Single email entry of an outbound contact card.

SendContactPhone.title: SendContactPhone
SendContactPhone.description: Single phone entry of an outbound contact card.

caption.title: Caption
caption.description: Optional caption. Supports the same `@<number>` mention tokens as text bodies (normalized digits, echoed in `mentions`).

SendDocumentContent.title: SendDocumentContent
SendDocumentContent.description: Send a document (PDF, DOCX, XLSX, etc.) via a public URL.

caption.title: Caption
caption.description: Optional caption. Supports the same `@<number>` mention tokens as text bodies (normalized digits, echoed in `mentions`).

SendImageContent.title: SendImageContent
SendImageContent.description: Send an image via a public URL. WhatsApp supports JPEG, PNG, WebP.

SendInteractiveContent.title: SendInteractiveContent
SendInteractiveContent.description:
Interactive message with a call-to-action URL button.

``interactive_type`` has a single accepted value today and ``url_button``
is required. Only the call-to-action URL button is supported.

SendLocationContent.title: SendLocationContent
SendLocationContent.description: Pin a geographic point as a WhatsApp location message.

SendMessageRequest.title: SendMessageRequest
SendMessageRequest.description:
``POST /v1/messages`` request body.

``to`` identifies the recipient (a phone, a group or a contact).
``content`` is the message itself; its kind is inferred from the fields
you send (see the content variants of this request).
``quoted_message_id`` is optional: give a ``msg_...`` id to quote an
existing message without using the dedicated ``/reply`` endpoint.

The sending number is the ``{alias}`` in the URL of
``POST /v1/numbers/{alias}/messages`` (``main`` on ``POST /v1/messages``),
so the body has no ``from`` field.

SendStickerContent.title: SendStickerContent
SendStickerContent.description:
Send a sticker via a public URL (animated WebP recommended).

WhatsApp does not show captions on stickers, so this content has no
``caption`` field (a caption would be silently lost).

text.title: Text
text.description: Message body. `@<number>` tokens (7-15 digits, e.g. `@5511990000001`) become real WhatsApp @mentions of that user: detected implicitly, normalized to canonical E.164 digits, and echoed in the message's `mentions` structure.

caption.title: Caption
caption.description: Optional caption. Supports the same `@<number>` mention tokens as text bodies (normalized digits, echoed in `mentions`).

SendVideoContent.title: SendVideoContent
SendVideoContent.description: Send a video via a public URL. WhatsApp supports MP4, 3GPP.

StorageSetupHint.title: StorageSetupHint
StorageSetupHint.description:
How to fix the storage, sent with unavailable media or pictures.

Present only when ``reason`` is ``"no_storage"`` or
``"storage_circuit_open"``: the cases where the organization can act
(configure or fix its storage). It is absent on ``upload_failed``, a
one-off failure where the storage is configured and the hint would
mislead.

Fields:
    setup_url: Deep link into the dashboard storage-setup flow.
    docs_url: Link to the public documentation page for BYO Object
        Storage configuration.
    message: Short English seed string suitable for display or
        further localisation (e.g. ``"Configure your media storage
        to receive inbound media files."``).

external_id.title: External Id
external_id.description: Your own identifier for this number (1 to 128 characters). Send a string to set or change it, `null` to remove it, or leave the field out to keep it. Another number of your account already using it answers 409 `external_id_already_used`.

UpdateExtraNumberRequest.title: UpdateExtraNumberRequest
UpdateExtraNumberRequest.description:
Send only the fields you want to change.

On the main number only `external_id` can be changed.

external_id.title: External Id
external_id.description: Your own identifier for this number, for example the id of the customer it serves in your system. 1 to 128 characters, surrounding spaces removed, no control characters. Unique among the numbers of your account; `null` when not set. Unlike `alias`, it can be any text (a UUID or an integer sent as a string) and it does not change when you rename the number.
